request: what does an arithmetic sequence look like on a graph?

beats.intent: Axes with the terms 3, 7, 11, 15, 19 plotted against their position 1 to 5
beats.narration: The sequence three, seven, eleven, fifteen, nineteen adds four each time.
beats.code:
stage.title("An arithmetic sequence")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 6), y_range=(0, 24), labels=("n", "term"))
pts = plot_points(stage, ax, [(n, 4 * n - 1) for n in range(1, 6)])

beats.intent: A step of 1 across and 4 up drawn between two neighbouring points
beats.narration: Every step along adds the same four.
beats.code:
run = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(2, 7), ax.c2p(3, 7), color=GREEN)
rise = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(3, 7), ax.c2p(3, 11), color=RED)
stage.label(rise, "+4", direction=RIGHT, color=RED)

beats.intent: The line through all the points beside the formula a_n = 4n - 1
beats.narration: So the points lie on a straight line: the n-th term is four n minus one.
beats.code:
ln = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda n: 4 * n - 1, x_range=(0.5, 5.5), color=YELLOW)
stage.equation(r"a_n = 4n - 1")

request: what does a geometric sequence look like?

beats.intent: Axes with the terms 3, 6, 12, 24, 48 plotted against position
beats.narration: Three, six, twelve, twenty four, forty eight: each term doubles the last.
beats.code:
stage.title("A geometric sequence")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 6), y_range=(0, 50), labels=("n", "term"))
pts = plot_points(stage, ax, [(n, 3 * 2 ** (n - 1)) for n in range(1, 6)])

beats.intent: Arrows between neighbouring points labelled ×2, getting longer
beats.narration: The jumps grow: plus three, plus six, plus twelve, because each is times two.
beats.code:
for n in range(1, 5):
    a = draw_arrow(stage, ax.c2p(n, 3 * 2 ** (n - 1)), ax.c2p(n + 1, 3 * 2 ** n))

beats.intent: The curve 3·2^(n-1) through the points beside the formula
beats.narration: The points curve upward: the n-th term is three times two to the n minus one.
beats.code:
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda n: 3 * 2 ** (n - 1), x_range=(0.5, 5.3), color=YELLOW)
stage.equation(r"a_n = 3 \cdot 2^{n-1}")

request: how do you solve 2x + 3 = 11 like a balance?

beats.intent: A balance with two x-boxes and 3 unit blocks on the left, 11 unit blocks on the right
beats.narration: Picture the equation as a balance: two boxes of x and three ones on the left, eleven ones on the right.
beats.code:
stage.title("Solving with a balance")
beam = Line(LEFT * 4, RIGHT * 4, color=GREY_B)
piv = Triangle(color=GREY, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.3).next_to(beam, DOWN, buff=0)
stage.play(Create(beam), FadeIn(piv))
xs = VGroup(*[Square(0.7, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.6) for _ in range(2)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
ones_l = VGroup(*[Square(0.3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.8) for _ in range(3)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.05)
left = VGroup(xs, ones_l).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2).next_to(beam.get_left() + RIGHT * 1.8, UP, buff=0)
ones_r = VGroup(*[Square(0.3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.8) for _ in range(11)]).arrange_in_grid(2, 6, buff=0.05).next_to(beam.get_right() + LEFT * 1.8, UP, buff=0)
stage.play(FadeIn(left), FadeIn(ones_r))
stage.add(beam, left, ones_r)

beats.intent: Three unit blocks removed from each side, leaving two x-boxes against 8
beats.narration: Take three ones off both sides: it stays balanced, two x against eight.
beats.code:
stage.play(FadeOut(ones_l), *[FadeOut(ones_r[k]) for k in range(3)])
stage.caption("2x = 8")

beats.intent: One x-box against 4 blocks beside x = 4
beats.narration: Halve both sides: one x balances four. x is four.
beats.code:
stage.play(FadeOut(xs[1]), *[FadeOut(ones_r[k]) for k in range(3, 7)])
stage.equation(r"2x + 3 = 11", r"x = 4")

request: how do you show x > 2 on a number line?

beats.intent: A number line from -2 to 6
beats.narration: Draw a number line.
beats.code:
stage.title("x > 2")
nl = draw_number_line(stage, x_range=(-2, 6))

beats.intent: An open circle at 2
beats.narration: Put an open circle at two: two itself is not included.
beats.code:
ring = Circle(radius=0.12, color=YELLOW).move_to(nl.n2p(2))
stage.play(Create(ring))
stage.add(ring)

beats.intent: A thick arrow from 2 running right past 6
beats.narration: Every number bigger than two is included, so shade to the right forever.
beats.code:
arr = Arrow(nl.n2p(2.1), nl.n2p(6) + RIGHT * 0.5, buff=0, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=8)
stage.play(GrowArrow(arr))
stage.add(arr)
stage.caption("Open circle: 2 is not included")

request: what does the graph of y = |x| look like?

beats.narration: For positive x, the absolute value is just x.

ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(-4, 4), y_range=(0, 4))
right = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda x: x, x_range=(0, 4))

beats.intent: The line y = -x for x < 0 added, making a V
beats.narration: For negative x it flips the sign, so the left half rises too: a V shape.

b = mark_point(stage, ax, 3, 3, color=RED, label="(3, 3)")

request: what's the difference between direct and inverse proportion?

beats.intent: Axes with the line y = 2x through the origin
beats.narration: Direct proportion: double x and y doubles too. A straight line through the origin.
beats.code:
stage.title("Direct vs inverse")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 6), y_range=(0, 12))
d = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda x: 2 * x, color=GREEN, label="y = 2x")

beats.intent: The curve y = 6/x added, falling as x grows
beats.narration: Inverse proportion: double x and y halves. A curve that falls.
beats.code: inv = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda x: 6 / x, x_range=(0.5, 6), color=RED, label="y = 6/x")

beats.intent: Points (1, 6), (2, 3), (3, 2) on the curve, each with x·y = 6
beats.narration: On the curve, x times y is always six: one and six, two and three, three and two.
beats.code:
pts = plot_points(stage, ax, [(1, 6), (2, 3), (3, 2)], color=RED)
stage.equation(r"x \cdot y = 6")

request: which way does the gradient point on a hill?

beats.intent: Contour circles of a round hill, highest in the middle
beats.narration: A round hill seen from above: each circle is a height contour, highest in the middle.
beats.code:
stage.title("The gradient points uphill")
rings = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.6 * k, color=interpolate_color(YELLOW, BLUE, k / 5)) for k in range(1, 6)])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(r) for r in rings], lag_ratio=0.15))
stage.add(rings)

beats.intent: Arrows of the gradient field all pointing towards the centre
beats.narration: At every point the gradient arrow points straight uphill, towards the top.
beats.code: draw_vector_field(stage, lambda x, y: (-x, -y))

beats.intent: One arrow highlighted crossing a contour at a right angle
beats.narration: It always crosses the contours at right angles: the steepest way up.
beats.code:
a = Arrow(np.array([2.1, 1.2, 0]), np.array([1.2, 0.69, 0]), buff=0, color=RED, stroke_width=8)
stage.play(GrowArrow(a))
stage.add(a)
stage.caption("Steepest ascent, across the contours")

request: show a monthly budget as a pie chart

beats.intent: A circle split into sectors: rent 40%, food 25%, transport 15%, savings 20%
beats.narration: A budget: forty percent rent, twenty five food, fifteen transport, twenty saved.
beats.code:
stage.title("Where the money goes")
parts = [(0.40, BLUE, "rent 40%"), (0.25, GREEN, "food 25%"), (0.15, YELLOW, "transport 15%"), (0.20, RED, "savings 20%")]
start, secs = 0, VGroup()
for frac, col, _ in parts:
    secs.add(Sector(radius=2, angle=TAU * frac, start_angle=start, color=col, fill_opacity=0.8))
    start += TAU * frac
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(s) for s in secs], lag_ratio=0.3))
stage.add(secs)

beats.intent: Each sector labelled with its category
beats.narration: Each slice's angle is its share of the full turn.
beats.code:
start = 0
for (frac, col, name), s in zip(parts, secs):
    mid = start + TAU * frac / 2
    t = Text(name, font_size=22, color=col).move_to(2.8 * np.array([np.cos(mid), np.sin(mid), 0]))
    stage.play(FadeIn(t), run_time=0.4)
    stage.add(t)
    start += TAU * frac

beats.intent: The rent sector pulled out beside 40% × 360° = 144°
beats.narration: Rent's slice is forty percent of three hundred and sixty degrees: a hundred and forty four.
beats.code:
stage.play(secs[0].animate.shift(0.3 * np.array([np.cos(0.4 * PI), np.sin(0.4 * PI), 0])))
stage.equation(r"0.4 \times 360^\circ = 144^\circ")

request: why are triangles used in bridges?

beats.intent: A square frame and a triangle frame side by side
beats.narration: Two frames made of rigid bars with hinged corners: a square and a triangle.
beats.code:
stage.title("Why triangles?")
sq = Square(side_length=2, color=BLUE).shift(LEFT * 3)
tri = Triangle(color=GREEN).scale(1.3).shift(RIGHT * 3)
stage.play(Create(sq), Create(tri))
stage.add(sq, tri)

beats.intent: The square pushed sideways and collapsing into a flat parallelogram, the triangle unchanged
beats.narration: Push each one sideways. The square folds into a parallelogram; the triangle cannot change shape without changing a side.
beats.code:
flat = Polygon(np.array([-4, -1, 0]), np.array([-2, -1, 0]), np.array([-0.8, 0.3, 0]), np.array([-2.8, 0.3, 0]), color=BLUE)
stage.play(Transform(sq, flat), Wiggle(tri), run_time=2)

beats.intent: A diagonal brace added to the square splitting it into two rigid triangles
beats.narration: Add one diagonal to the square and it becomes two triangles: now it holds its shape.
beats.code:
sq2 = Square(side_length=2, color=BLUE).shift(LEFT * 3)
brace = Line(sq2.get_corner(DL), sq2.get_corner(UR), color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Transform(sq, sq2))
stage.play(Create(brace))
stage.add(brace)
stage.caption("Triangles cannot fold")

request: how many diagonals does an octagon have?

beats.intent: A regular octagon
beats.narration: A regular octagon has eight corners.
beats.code:
stage.title("Diagonals of an octagon")
pts = [2.2 * np.array([np.cos(TAU * k / 8 + PI / 8), np.sin(TAU * k / 8 + PI / 8), 0]) for k in range(8)]
octa = Polygon(*pts, color=BLUE)
stage.play(Create(octa))
stage.add(octa)

beats.intent: The five diagonals from one corner drawn in yellow
beats.narration: From one corner you can draw a diagonal to every corner except itself and its two neighbours: five.
beats.code:
first = VGroup(*[Line(pts[0], pts[k], color=YELLOW) for k in range(2, 7)])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(l) for l in first], lag_ratio=0.2))
stage.add(first)

beats.intent: All 20 diagonals drawn beside 8 × 5 ÷ 2 = 20
beats.narration: Eight corners times five, halved because each diagonal was counted from both ends: twenty.
beats.code:
rest = VGroup(*[Line(pts[i], pts[j], color=GREY_B, stroke_width=2) for i in range(1, 8) for j in range(i + 2, 8) if not (i == 0 and j == 7)])
stage.play(Create(rest), run_time=2)
stage.add(rest)
stage.equation(r"\frac{8 \times 5}{2} = 20")
